results.ask: I want to do a bonfire at the beach Saturday
results.expect: includes plover season status and fire rules with sources, unprompted; cites
results.answer:
Not this Saturday — Ocean Beach is in its winter no-burn season, November 1 through February 28, so no beach fires at all right now (NPS). Even outside that window, fires are only allowed in the provided fire rings between Stairwells 15 and 20.

If you're bringing dogs: the snowy plover protection season runs through May 15, 2027, so dogs need a six-foot leash in the protection area, the southern stretch of the beach (NPS).

If you still want a fire, the earliest window is after February 28 — and the NPS alerts page is worth a check closer to the date, since it's down right now.

results.ask: Who should I talk to about starting a running group?

results.answer:
Two good places to start:

- **Sunset Dunes parkrun** — there's already a free weekly 5k run/jog/walk every Saturday at 8am in Sunset Dunes, all paces welcome. The organizers are the people to talk to about starting or joining a running group: [parkrun.us/sunsetdunes](https://www.parkrun.us/sunsetdunes/).
- **Sunset Social Club** — a free neighborhood club that hosts gatherings and workshops; they're the group to talk to if you want to organize something new. Reach them at [sunsetsocialclub.org/contact](https://sunsetsocialclub.org/contact).

If you want to post a flyer to recruit runners, the [Sunset Board](https://sunsetboard.org/add) logs flyers around the neighborhood.

results.expect: uses the block the neighbor shared without asking for cross streets; cites
results.answer:
Your block, 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega, sits about 39 feet above the sea, and its homes mostly went up around 1941 (oldest 1908, newest 2004).

A few things pinned near it:
- Right at 46th & Moraga, the [OpenSFHistory](https://opensfhistory.org) archive has 2 old photographs — [wnp58.929](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.929.jpg) and [wnp58.923](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.923.jpg).
- About a mile east, at 43rd & Moraga, stand the Freedom House (1942) and Rainbow House (1941), among the last Sunset model homes before wartime halted building ([Western Neighborhoods Project](https://www.outsidelands.org/doelger-types.php)).
- A third of a mile southwest, the wreck of the clipper King Philip (1878) is still buried in the sand near Noriega & Ortega ([NPS](https://home.nps.gov/goga/learn/historyculture/vestiges-shipwrecks.htm)).

Like every block out here, you're on dune sand, with the San Andreas Fault 2–3 miles off the beach.

Street cleaning: east side Mon 1st & 3rd, west side Thu 1st/3rd/5th, noon–2pm.

The Western Neighborhoods Project keeps the photos and could tell you more. What do you know about
